perf_budget_class_justification: tick_once is a periodic supervisor loop (cadence = heartbeat_interval_secs, not sub-millisecond). The four declared budgets (idle-tick p95 ≤25 tok, restart p95 ≤1500ms, RSS ≤64MiB, watchdog-kill p95 ≤5000ms) are consistent with warm-path characterisation. The watchdog-kill sub-path is cold-path (error recovery). v5 SettingsRenderer::verify introduces filesystem I/O into snapshot() which is called at step 2 of every tick_once — this threatens to push the snapshot() sub-path from warm toward cold, especially at N>1 accounts.
benchmark_harness: std::time::Instant (zero-dep, no criterion — Branch Y constraint, §B.1 + §A.5 note)
regression_baseline_justification: All four new crates (supervisor-kernel, supervisor-app, jsonl-supervisor-adapter, supervisor-conformance) are net-new scaffold artifacts — no prior implementation exists. The heartbeat.rs harness will produce first-run values that become the baseline. There is no claude-heartbeat-equivalent historical series to compare against; the 'reference shape' (Siigari/claude-heartbeat) is a behavioural reference, not a numeric perf baseline. The first cargo-bench run at branch-Y supervisor-v4 baseline establishes the floor.
verdict_summary: v4 core warm-path is acceptably designed for the declared load profile. Two BLOCKER-grade gaps require fixup before merge: (1) v5 introduces unbounded filesystem I/O (file-reads + blake3) into AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot(), which is called every tick_once, with no debounce TTL or latency budget declared for the verify path; (2) the bench harness (std::time::Instant, zero-dep) cannot compute statistically valid p95 values — C.13a-d p95 claims are unverifiable as specified. Three WARNING-grade findings also noted.

findings.summary: v5 SettingsRenderer::verify introduces O(3N) filesystem I/O on every tick_once with no debounce TTL, no latency budget, and no bench coverage
findings.detail: v5 §B.4 wires CompositeAccountSnapshotProvider to call SettingsRenderer::verify for each ProviderAccount inside AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot(). snapshot() is invoked at step 2 of every tick_once (§B.4 call chain). verify() reads each rendered file from disk and computes a blake3 hash per RenderedFile (§B.2.1 RenderedFile.content_blake3 [u8;32]). For N accounts × 3 providers this is O(3N) filesystem reads + O(3N) blake3 passes per tick. No debounce TTL, no cache, no last-verified timestamp is declared anywhere in v5. The existing C.13a (idle-tick p95 ≤25 tok) and C.13b (restart p95 ≤1500ms) budgets were declared in v4 before v5 existed; they do not cover the verify path. v5 §C.25–C.30 adds only correctness rows (C.27 drift detection, C.28 idempotency) with no latency budget for verify(). At 10× account count (30 accounts, 90 file reads per tick) this will silently blow the idle-tick budget and may violate restart latency. Anti-pattern: alloc-on-hot-path-without-bench + tail-latency-not-measured.
findings.at_10x_load: 90 file reads + 90 blake3 hashes per tick. On a 7200rpm HDD (150 IOPS), this alone consumes ~600ms/tick — well past the restart p95 ≤1500ms budget. Even on NVMe (100µs/read) it adds ~9ms per tick, pushing idle-tick above 25-token proxy. The verify path is not bounded by the existing bench.
findings.fixuptask_recommendation: Add a VerifyDebounce mechanism: track last_verified_at per (ProviderAccount, ProviderFamily); skip verify() if elapsed < verify_ttl_secs (configurable, default 60s). Add acceptance row C.31: 'tick_once with 10 accounts × 3 providers completes snapshot() in ≤50ms p99 when no files have changed (debounce hot-path).' Add bench sub-metric verify_snapshot_p99_ms to heartbeat.rs.

findings.summary: Bench harness (std::time::Instant, no criterion) cannot produce statistically valid p95 values; C.13a-d p95 claims are unverifiable as specified
findings.detail: v4 §B.1 and §A.5 note: 'harness uses std::time::Instant only; emits one JSONL row per metric per the schema declared in §C.13. Bench-bin is driven by cargo test --release --bench heartbeat to stay zero-dep.' A single Instant measurement per metric produces a single sample, not a distribution. p95 requires a minimum of ~20 samples (exact: ceil(1/(1-0.95)) = 20) for any meaningful quantile estimate; robust p95 needs ≥100 samples with outlier handling. The JSONL schema emits {"metric":"idle_tick_p95_tokens","value":<n>,"p":95} — but if value is from a single measurement or small fixed loop, the 'p':95 label is false precision. C.13a-d gate conditions (value ≤25, ≤1500, ≤65536, ≤5000) will pass based on a lucky single warm-cache run, not representative tail behaviour. Anti-pattern: perf-claim-without-benchmark.
findings.fixuptask_recommendation: Declare an explicit iteration count in heartbeat.rs: run each sub-bench ≥200 iterations, collect all durations into a Vec<u64>, sort, emit true p50/p95/p99. Alternatively, declare the harness as 'best-effort latency sample' (not p95) and rename the JSONL fields accordingly (metric: idle_tick_sample_ms). Either path is acceptable under Branch Y; the false-precision p95 label is not. Update C.13a-d acceptance criteria to match the actual harness semantics.

findings.summary: SessionTicket and Vec<ProviderAccount> allocated fresh on every tick_once — no pooling declared
findings.detail: tick_once step 2 calls self.accounts.snapshot() returning Vec<ProviderAccount> — heap allocation per tick regardless of whether the account set has changed. Step 13 constructs a new SessionTicket (8 owned fields: MessageId(String), RequestId(String), AccountId(String), ProviderFamily(enum), AutonomyTier(enum), UsageWindowSnapshot(7 fields), cost_ceiling_tokens(u64), model_hint(String)) and passes it as SessionVerdict::Spawn { ticket: SessionTicket }. The ticket String fields (MessageId, RequestId, model_hint) require two heap allocations per tick minimum. For warm-path supervisor use (one tick per heartbeat) this is acceptable. At saturated mode (back-to-back ticks draining a deep inbox), allocations accumulate without a reclaim path. No pool or arena is declared.
findings.allocation_count_note: minimum per tick: Vec<ProviderAccount> + MessageId(String) + RequestId(String)/model_hint(String). Actual count higher when UsageWindowSnapshot.kind_label String is populated.
findings.fixuptask_recommendation: Not required for initial impl at declared load profile (single-supervisor, heartbeat cadence). Revisit when M02-P02 multi-subscription-pool drives back-to-back ticks. Document allocation profile in heartbeat.rs bench output as a tracking metric.

findings.summary: UsageWindow::clone() at step 7.5 is an unconditional pre-flight projection clone on every tick decision path
findings.detail: v4 §B.4 step 7.5: 'let mut projected: UsageWindow = window.clone()' runs unconditionally before the live check_limit call. UsageWindow is declared at account-domain:252 with 'fields all owned numeric/enum' (verified §B.0 row). The clone is cheap (no heap String fields visible in the plan description) but is performed even on the early-exit Saturated path — although Saturated returns before step 1's peek_lock, so the clone at 7.5 is only reached after a message is locked. Acceptable for warm-path. No concern at current load; flagged for awareness.
findings.allocation_count_note: One UsageWindow stack/heap copy per non-saturated tick. Cost depends on UsageWindow field layout (account-domain:252 — plan says 'owned numeric/enum', implying stack-copyable or shallow heap).

findings.summary: projected_tokens_p95 rolling window reads and parses inbox/.../stats.jsonl on every non-saturated tick with no in-memory cache declared
findings.detail: v4 §B.6: 'projected_tokens_p95 is computed from a per-(provider, model_hint) rolling window of the last 100 observed tokens_in + tokens_out, persisted in inbox/.../stats.jsonl.' The plan does not specify whether this file is read and re-parsed on every tick_once or cached in memory. If re-read per tick, this adds a file read + hand-rolled parse pass (up to 100 JSONL lines × ~80 bytes each = ~8KB) on every decision. The conservative seed (n<10: projected=cost_ceiling_tokens) avoids I/O on cold-start — correct. For warm operation (n≥10) the I/O is on the critical path between steps 7 and 13. No acceptance row in C.1–C.24 verifies the stats.jsonl read latency contribution. Should be declared as an in-memory cache with file-persistence for durability.
findings.fixuptask_recommendation: Declare in-memory cache for the rolling window (100-entry ring buffer per (provider, model_hint) key, persisted to stats.jsonl only on write, not on read). Add a note to C.19 or a new row specifying that projected_tokens_p95 is computed from the in-memory ring buffer, not a per-tick file parse.

C13a_idle_tick_p95_tokens.v5_impact: UNCOVERED — v5 verify path adds filesystem I/O to snapshot() which is inside tick_once; C.13a budget was declared pre-v5 and does not account for verify latency

C13b_restart_latency_p95_ms.v5_impact: UNCOVERED — same as C.13a; verify() during snapshot() adds to restart path

C13c_rss_max_kib.v5_impact: LOW — v5 types (SettingsTemplate, DriftReport) are value types; no large in-memory buffers declared; blake3 is stack-computed

C13d_watchdog_kill_p95_ms.v5_impact: NONE — watchdog path does not traverse snapshot()

v5_verify_latency.v5_impact: NO BUDGET DECLARED — this is the primary gap

anti_patterns_triggered.location: v5 verify path: no latency budget row in C.25–C.30
heartbeat.rs §C.13a-d p95 claims from std::time::Instant single-sample harness

zero_copy_assessment.detail: v4 Principle 3 (value-only-tickets) is the right call for correctness and safety across blocking-pool boundaries. The clone cost is justified. No zero-copy opportunity was sacrificed unnecessarily in v4. v5 SettingsRenderer::verify does read file bytes into owned Vec<u8> buffers for blake3 — this is unavoidable for hash comparison but is unguarded by debounce.

mutex_hot_path_assessment.detail: tick_once Saturated fast-path: self.in_flight_permits.try_acquire() is a non-blocking tokio semaphore check (atomic CAS). At heartbeat cadence this is not contended. At 10× load with concurrent tick_once invocations the semaphore is the correct back-pressure mechanism and its contention cost is dominated by I/O elsewhere. No mutex-on-hot-path-without-justification anti-pattern triggered.
